quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You may only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no traffic crossing.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if a sign does not prohibit it.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of them quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down when passing a bicycle and give them plenty of space. Bicyclists have less protection than drivers. Passing too quickly can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: What parts of your vehicle must you clear of snow and ice before driving?

options.text: The windows.
The hood.
The top.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must remove all snow and ice from your entire vehicle before driving. You may be fined if you do not follow this law.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in rain?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?

options.text: Only the driver.
Only adult passengers.
Only child passengers.
Everyone in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: The driver and all passengers must wear a seat belt. It is illegal for the driver, front seat passengers, or anyone under 18 to not wear a seat belt. The driver is responsible for all passengers under 18. Back seat passengers 18 and older can also be fined if not buckled.

questions.question: When can you NOT cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is broken down.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if it is safe and you do not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing the radio or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers must make many decisions every mile. Any extra activity takes your attention away from driving and creates danger.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will turn sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols on yellow background. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns that pedestrians may cross the road.

questions.question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Keep the car straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas pedal.
Keep your current speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slow down by taking your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car going straight. Take your foot off the gas pedal. Do not brake until you have control of the car. Once the car is stable, brake gently and pull over safely.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing in front of your car. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful around children. Always let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed on a road under dangerous conditions.
The highest or lowest legal speed on a road under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed on a road under ideal conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed on a road under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under ideal conditions. You can drive slower than the posted limit, but driving faster is illegal. Drive slower in school zones and work zones. If weather or road construction makes the posted speed unsafe, drive slower.

questions.question: When you drive while distracted, what usually happens?

options.text: It is never dangerous.
You react more slowly to hazards.
You usually drive faster.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow down how fast you react to traffic and road hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.
Not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on overcast days. Use your low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming car or within 500 feet of a car ahead of you. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level above the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach an unmarked railroad crossing. Look both ways to make sure no trains are coming from either direction. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait until it passes before crossing.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving
Driving too fast for conditions
Following other cars too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Following too closely causes most rear-end collisions.

questions.question: Your blind spot is an area you cannot see without:

options.text: Moving your head.
Looking directly behind your car.
Using your rearview mirror.
Using your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Moving your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your car.

questions.question: If you drive with a suspended license and cause an accident that injures someone, what can happen?

options.text: You will receive a warning.
You will only be fined.
You may be fined, have your license suspended longer, and go to jail.
You will get points on your license.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be fined, have your license suspended longer, and go to jail.
questions.explanation: Driving with a suspended license is illegal. If you do this, you will pay a fine, go to jail for up to 45 days, and have your license suspended for a longer time.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
The road is slippery when wet.
The road curves ahead.
A hill is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right, you must let that vehicle go first. You may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: You are backing out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Honk your horn so children hear you.
Walk to the back of your car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of your car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing up. Do not rely only on your mirrors, especially when children are nearby.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Then you may proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they see an animal on the road?

options.text: No special action is needed.
Honk the horn.
Pass the animal as closely as possible.
Be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid startling it.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: Less dangerous.
Just as dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see, headlights from other cars can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Drive carefully and watch for children and pedestrians in these areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Keep right.
No U-turn.
Left lane must turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed. Regulation signs show rules that drivers must follow.

questions.question: A school bus has stopped with its stop arm extended. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk before passing on the left.
Continue when you think kids are done exiting.
Pass before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When a school bus stops with its stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop. Do not proceed until the stop arm is pulled back.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with a siren and/or flashing lights approaches you, what must you do immediately?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights, sirens, or other warning devices approaches, you must immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: When may you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: You should use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to a dangerous situation.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Which vehicle has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle approaching from the right.
The vehicle approaching from the left.
The vehicle whose driver sounds the horn first.
The vehicle traveling the fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle approaching from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without traffic signals, you must yield to any vehicle approaching from your right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road narrows ahead.
There are several curves ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are several curves ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has three or more curves.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not slam on the brakes. Grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Release the accelerator and slow down gradually. Once moving slowly, apply the brakes lightly and move to a safe area off the road.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you start to slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
When you see a toll booth.
After you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane well ahead of time. Do not begin slowing down until after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to use:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The full lane width, the same as other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The sidewalk width.

questions.correctAnswerText: The full lane width, the same as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the full width of a traffic lane, just like all other vehicles.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel hard to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down with gentle braking. Turn the steering wheel gradually to return to the pavement safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down with gentle braking. Turn the steering wheel gradually to return to the pavement safely.
questions.explanation: Keep the wheels off the pavement and reduce speed by gently applying the brakes. When at a safe speed, gradually turn the steering wheel to return to the road. Do not jerk the steering wheel.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, where should you grip the steering wheel?

options.text: At 1 o'clock and 11 o'clock.
At 2 o'clock and 10 o'clock.
At 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock.
At 5 o'clock and 7 o'clock.

questions.correctAnswerText: At 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock.
questions.explanation: Think of the steering wheel as a clock face. Grip the outside edge at the 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock positions with your thumbs along the face of the wheel.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop and wait for any vehicles or pedestrians to pass before you proceed.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street in the wrong direction.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Drivers turning left on a green light must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers turning left on a green light must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way. Wait for oncoming traffic to pass before turning.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down but do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure it is not headed toward you.

questions.question: To register a vehicle in New Jersey, you must be age ____ or older.
questions.explanation: You must be at least 17 years old to register a motor vehicle in New Jersey. You will need proof of identity and proof of vehicle ownership.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive the same way as on dry roads.
Keep a greater distance between you and the car ahead.
Avoid crossing bridges or intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a greater distance between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. Your vehicle will take longer to stop under these conditions.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your emergency signals or horn when needed.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is hurt. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you have to. Moving them incorrectly can make injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop the bleeding.

questions.question: You notice a vehicle defect that affects safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you can afford it.
Drive at slower speeds.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that affects safe driving as soon as possible. Do not drive the vehicle until the defect is corrected.

questions.question: What does this sign prevent?

options.text: Entry to full parking lots.
Entry to road construction areas.
Entry to dead-end streets.
Entry from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entry from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic only moves one way. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: On high beam.
On low beam.
Off, with parking lights on.
On either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: On low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when another vehicle is coming toward you or when you are following another vehicle. Use low beam to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: What do orange-colored signs indicate?

options.text: Work zone signs.
Regulatory signs.
School zone signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones on highways. These diamond-shaped signs have black letters or symbols and warn you that people are working on or near the road.
